questions.title: What is an EntityType, and what are its keys, properties, and navigation properties (associations)?
questions.description: An EntityType describes the structure of one kind of business object that an OData service offers, like Product, Customer or SalesOrder, similar to a table definition in a database or a class in programming. It is defined in the service metadata ($metadata) and has three main parts. Properties are the fields of the entity, each with a name, a data type (like Edm.String or Edm.Decimal), and facets such as Nullable, MaxLength, or Precision and Scale. The Key lists one or more PropertyRef elements: the properties that together identify one entity uniquely, like ProductID, or SalesOrderID plus ItemPosition for an order item; the key values are what appears in an entity's URL, like Products('HT-1000'). Navigation properties describe relationships to other entity types, like a product's ToSupplier or an order's ToItems. In OData V2, each navigation property is based on an Association, a separate definition that names the two ends (roles) and their multiplicities (1, 0..1, or * for many), and an AssociationSet connects the entity sets. Navigation properties are what make paths like /Products('HT-1000')/ToSupplier and the $expand option possible.
keyPoints: An EntityType defines the structure of one kind of business object (like a table definition).
Properties: name, Edm data type, and facets (Nullable, MaxLength, Precision, Scale...).
Key: the PropertyRefs that uniquely identify an entity; they appear in its URL.
NavigationProperty: a relationship to another entity type, based on an Association (roles and multiplicities) in V2.

examples.title: An EntityType in $metadata
examples.code:
<edmx:Edmx Version="1.0" xmlns:edmx="http://schemas.microsoft.com/ado/2007/06/edmx"
  xmlns:m="http://schemas.microsoft.com/ado/2007/08/dataservices/metadata"
  xmlns:sap="http://www.sap.com/Protocols/SAPData">
  <edmx:DataServices m:DataServiceVersion="2.0">
    <Schema Namespace="ZSHOP_SRV" xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/ado/2008/09/edm">
      <EntityType Name="Product" sap:content-version="1">
        <Key>
          <PropertyRef Name="ProductID" />
        </Key>
        <Property Name="ProductID" Type="Edm.String" Nullable="false" MaxLength="10" sap:label="Product ID" />
        <Property Name="Name" Type="Edm.String" MaxLength="80" sap:label="Name" />
        <Property Name="Price" Type="Edm.Decimal" Precision="15" Scale="2" sap:unit="Currency" />
        <Property Name="Currency" Type="Edm.String" MaxLength="5" sap:semantics="currency-code" />
        <Property Name="SupplierID" Type="Edm.String" MaxLength="10" />
        <NavigationProperty Name="ToSupplier" Relationship="ZSHOP_SRV.Product_Supplier"
          FromRole="FromRole_Product" ToRole="ToRole_Supplier" />
      </EntityType>
    </Schema>
  </edmx:DataServices>
</edmx:Edmx>

questions.title: What is an EntitySet?
questions.description: An EntitySet is the collection of all entities of one EntityType that the service exposes, so it is what you actually address in a URL. If the EntityType Product describes what a product looks like, the EntitySet Products (often named in the plural) is the list of products you can read, filter, create in, and so on: GET /Products returns the collection, and GET /Products('HT-1000') returns one entity from it. In the metadata, entity sets are declared inside the EntityContainer, each with its name and EntityType, like <EntitySet Name="Products" EntityType="ZSHOP_SRV.Product" />. An entity type can be exposed in more than one entity set, although usually there is one per type. SAP services add attributes to the entity set that describe what is allowed, like sap:creatable, sap:updatable, sap:deletable, sap:pageable or sap:addressable. In UI5, binding paths start with an entity set, like items="{/Products}" for a list or /Products('HT-1000') for one object. The EntityContainer also holds the AssociationSets and the FunctionImports of the service.
keyPoints: An EntitySet is the collection of all entities of one EntityType that the service exposes.
It is what URLs address: /Products (collection), /Products('HT-1000') (one entity).
Declared in the EntityContainer: <EntitySet Name="Products" EntityType="ns.Product" />.
SAP attributes like sap:creatable / sap:updatable / sap:deletable describe allowed operations.

examples.title: The EntityContainer
examples.code:
<EntityContainer Name="ZSHOP_SRV_Entities" m:IsDefaultEntityContainer="true"
  xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/ado/2008/09/edm"
  xmlns:m="http://schemas.microsoft.com/ado/2007/08/dataservices/metadata"
  xmlns:sap="http://www.sap.com/Protocols/SAPData">
  <EntitySet Name="Products" EntityType="ZSHOP_SRV.Product"
    sap:creatable="true" sap:updatable="true" sap:deletable="false" sap:pageable="true" />
  <EntitySet Name="Suppliers" EntityType="ZSHOP_SRV.Supplier" />
  <AssociationSet Name="Product_Supplier_Set" Association="ZSHOP_SRV.Product_Supplier">
    <End EntitySet="Products" Role="FromRole_Product" />
    <End EntitySet="Suppliers" Role="ToRole_Supplier" />
  </AssociationSet>
</EntityContainer>

questions.title: What is a Function Import in the OData metadata?
questions.description: A Function Import is the metadata declaration of a custom operation that the service offers besides the standard CRUD operations, like ApproveOrder, ReleaseDocument or CalculatePrice. It is declared in the EntityContainer with a Name, an m:HttpMethod (GET for operations that only read or calculate, POST for operations that change data), its Parameters (each with a name, Edm type, and Mode="In"), and optionally a ReturnType: a single entity, a collection (Collection(ns.Product)), a complex type, or a simple type. When it returns entities, EntitySet names the set they belong to. SAP services can add sap:action-for to tie it to an entity type, and sap:applicable-path to make it available only for some entities. The client calls it by its name as a URL path segment, with the parameters as URL parameters, like POST /ApproveOrder?OrderID='4711'; in UI5 V2 with model.callFunction("/ApproveOrder", { method: "POST", urlParameters: { OrderID: "4711" } }). OData V4 replaces function imports with actions (that can change data) and functions (that cannot).
keyPoints: A Function Import declares a custom service operation beyond CRUD.
It has a Name, m:HttpMethod (GET or POST), Parameters, and an optional ReturnType (+ EntitySet).
Called as /Name?param='value'; in UI5 V2 with model.callFunction("/Name", {...}).
OData V4 replaces it with actions (may change data) and functions (read-only).

examples.title: A Function Import declaration
examples.code:
<FunctionImport Name="ApproveOrder" ReturnType="ZSHOP_SRV.SalesOrder" EntitySet="SalesOrders"
  m:HttpMethod="POST" sap:action-for="ZSHOP_SRV.SalesOrder"
  xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/ado/2008/09/edm"
  xmlns:m="http://schemas.microsoft.com/ado/2007/08/dataservices/metadata"
  xmlns:sap="http://www.sap.com/Protocols/SAPData">
  <Parameter Name="OrderID" Type="Edm.String" Mode="In" MaxLength="10" />
</FunctionImport>

questions.title: What are the main OData data types (Decimal, DateTime, Int, String), and what should you know about them?
questions.description: Every property in an OData V2 service has an EDM (Entity Data Model) type. Edm.String is text; its facet MaxLength limits the number of characters, which UI5 can use as the maximum input length. The integer types are Edm.Int16, Edm.Int32 and Edm.Int64 (and Edm.Byte); Int16 and Int32 arrive as JavaScript numbers, but Int64 values are sent as strings in JSON, because JavaScript numbers cannot represent all 64-bit integers exactly. Edm.Decimal is for exact decimal numbers like amounts and quantities; its facets Precision (total digits) and Scale (digits after the decimal point) describe the format, and its values are also sent as strings (like "1499.90"), to avoid floating-point rounding errors, so do not calculate with them as normal numbers without care. Edm.DateTime is a date and time without a time zone; in V2 JSON it looks like /Date(1700000000000)/, and UI5 converts it into a JavaScript Date. SAP services often mark date-only values with sap:display-format="Date". Edm.DateTimeOffset includes a time zone offset, and Edm.Time is a time of day. Others are Edm.Boolean, Edm.Guid, Edm.Double and Edm.Binary. UI5 has matching binding types in sap.ui.model.odata.type (like String, Int32, Decimal, DateTime), which respect the facets automatically.
keyPoints: Edm.String with MaxLength; Edm.Int16 / Int32 / Int64 (Int64 is sent as a string in JSON).
Edm.Decimal with Precision and Scale; values are strings to avoid rounding errors.
Edm.DateTime: no time zone, /Date(ms)/ in V2 JSON, converted to a JS Date; sap:display-format="Date" for dates.
Also DateTimeOffset, Time, Boolean, Guid; UI5's sap.ui.model.odata.type.* types follow the facets.

examples.title: Typed properties and how they arrive in JSON
examples.code:
<Property Name="Name"      Type="Edm.String"   MaxLength="80" />
<Property Name="Quantity"  Type="Edm.Int32" />
<Property Name="Price"     Type="Edm.Decimal"  Precision="15" Scale="2" />
<Property Name="CreatedAt" Type="Edm.DateTime" Precision="7" sap:display-format="Date" />

JSON (OData V2):
{ "Name": "Notebook", "Quantity": 3, "Price": "1499.90", "CreatedAt": "/Date(1700000000000)/" }

examples.title: Binding with OData types
examples.code:
<Input value="{ path: 'Price', type: 'sap.ui.model.odata.type.Decimal',
                constraints: { precision: 15, scale: 2 } }" />
<DatePicker value="{ path: 'CreatedAt', type: 'sap.ui.model.odata.type.DateTime',
                     constraints: { displayFormat: 'Date' } }" />

questions.title: What is a ComplexType?
questions.description: A ComplexType is a structured type, a group of properties, that has no key and therefore no identity of its own. It cannot be read or addressed on its own, and it is not in an entity set; it only exists as the type of a property inside an entity (or as the parameter or return type of a function import). A typical example is an Address with Street, City, PostalCode and Country, used as the property Address in a Customer and in a Supplier: the structure is defined once and reused. Compared with a navigation property to a separate entity, a complex property always belongs to its parent: it is loaded together with the entity, without $expand, and is saved together with it. In a binding path, you reach its fields with a slash, like /Customers('1')/Address/City. Complex types are also common as the return type of function imports, when an operation returns a structure that is not an entity, like a calculation result with several values. In the metadata, it is declared with <ComplexType Name="Address"> and used with Type="ns.Address" on a property.
keyPoints: A ComplexType is a structured group of properties without a key or identity of its own.
It is used as the type of a property inside an entity, or for function import parameters / results.
It is loaded and saved together with its parent entity, without $expand.
Its fields are reached with a path like /Customers('1')/Address/City.

examples.title: Declaring and using a ComplexType
examples.code:
<Schema Namespace="ZSHOP_SRV" xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/ado/2008/09/edm">
  <ComplexType Name="Address">
    <Property Name="Street" Type="Edm.String" MaxLength="60" />
    <Property Name="City" Type="Edm.String" MaxLength="40" />
    <Property Name="PostalCode" Type="Edm.String" MaxLength="10" />
  </ComplexType>
  <EntityType Name="Customer">
    <Key>
      <PropertyRef Name="CustomerID" />
    </Key>
    <Property Name="CustomerID" Type="Edm.String" Nullable="false" />
    <Property Name="Address" Type="ZSHOP_SRV.Address" Nullable="false" />
  </EntityType>
</Schema>

questions.title: What are the non-standard attributes (sap:...) that SAP defined in OData V2 metadata?
questions.description: The OData V2 standard does not describe everything a business UI needs, so SAP added its own attributes to the metadata, in the namespace http://www.sap.com/Protocols/SAPData (prefix sap:). SAP Gateway services generate them, and UI5's smart controls and SAP Fiori elements read them. On properties: sap:label (a translated label for the field), sap:quickinfo (a tooltip), sap:creatable and sap:updatable (whether the field can be set on create and changed later), sap:filterable and sap:sortable (whether it can be used in $filter and $orderby), sap:required-in-filter, sap:unit (names the property holding the unit or currency of an amount), sap:semantics (the meaning, like currency-code, unit-of-measure, email or tel), sap:text (names the property with a readable text for a code, like the name for a status code), sap:display-format (like Date or UpperCase), and sap:field-control (points to a property that decides dynamically whether the field is hidden, read-only, optional or mandatory). On entity sets: sap:creatable, sap:updatable, sap:deletable, sap:pageable, sap:addressable, sap:searchable (supports the search query option) and sap:requires-filter. On entity types: sap:content-version and sap:label. Many of these have equivalents in the newer vocabulary-based annotations (like Common.Label or Capabilities), which are used in OData V4.
keyPoints: SAP added sap:... attributes (namespace http://www.sap.com/Protocols/SAPData) to OData V2 metadata.
Properties: sap:label, sap:quickinfo, sap:creatable/updatable, sap:filterable/sortable, sap:unit, sap:semantics, sap:text, sap:display-format, sap:field-control.
Entity sets: sap:creatable/updatable/deletable, sap:pageable, sap:addressable, sap:searchable, sap:requires-filter.
Smart controls and Fiori elements read them; V4 uses vocabulary annotations (Common.Label, Capabilities...) instead.

examples.title: Properties with SAP attributes
examples.code:
<EntityType Name="SalesOrder"
  xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/ado/2008/09/edm"
  xmlns:sap="http://www.sap.com/Protocols/SAPData">
  <Key>
    <PropertyRef Name="SalesOrderID" />
  </Key>
  <Property Name="SalesOrderID" Type="Edm.String" MaxLength="10" Nullable="false"
    sap:label="Sales Order" sap:creatable="false" sap:updatable="false" />
  <Property Name="Status" Type="Edm.String" MaxLength="1"
    sap:label="Status" sap:text="StatusText" sap:filterable="true" />
  <Property Name="StatusText" Type="Edm.String" MaxLength="40" sap:filterable="false" />
  <Property Name="GrossAmount" Type="Edm.Decimal" Precision="15" Scale="2"
    sap:label="Gross Amount" sap:unit="CurrencyCode" />
  <Property Name="CurrencyCode" Type="Edm.String" MaxLength="5" sap:semantics="currency-code" />
</EntityType>
